action: Plan step 2, residue of the parameter-range kind, entry actions 1-4. Action 1, the finite version and its parameter: the parameter is the codimension q, and the finite version at codimension q is the statement W(q) that a McMullen local weight is nonnegative on every transverse cone type of codimension q that occurs at a face of a five-part hive polytope. No constant must stay uniform, the target being a decision. Action 2, the equivalence and its proof: by the hive theorem the polynomial P is the Ehrhart polynomial of the rational hive polytope H, by Ferudun's period-one dilation lemma the lattice local Euler-Maclaurin formula transfers to H, and that formula writes the coefficient of t^{D-q} as the sum over the faces of codimension q of the lattice volume of the face, which is nonnegative, times a weight depending only on the face's transverse cone; so W(q) implies that the coefficient of t^{D-q} is nonnegative for every five-part hive, and the claim of this attack follows from W(0), ..., W(D) with D <= 6. The converse is not claimed and is not needed. Each W(q) is finite because every transverse cone of a full-dimensional five-part hive is generated by a subset of the 27 primitive rhombus normals of N_5, and every transverse cone of a lower-dimensional one is the image of such a cone under the projection to the intrinsic lattice, of which there are again finitely many. Action 3, the side with a finite certificate: the true side, by a nonnegative weight vector on the finitely many cone types, checkable by exact rational arithmetic; the false side by one five-part triple, which the sibling attacks exclude for size at most 30 exhaustively and for sizes 31 to 200 by sampling. Action 4: the residue is passed to the enumeration and certification steps of this strategy.
output: Residue at rank five, exactly two items, both finite. (a) W(5) for full-dimensional hives: the weight on the five-dimensional transverse cones of edges, that is on the cone types spanned by subsets of the C(27, 5) = 80,730 five-normal tuples of N_5 and their closures; it controls the linear coefficient, the one coefficient of a full-dimensional five-part hive that Ferudun 2026 leaves open. (b) The non-full-dimensional five-part hives of intrinsic dimension three, four and five: their transverse cones are projections of N_5 to the intrinsic lattice, the published atlas does not cover them, and Horn factorisation does not reduce them to four parts, as the triple lam = (4,3,3,1), mu = (4,2,1,1), nu = (6,5,4,2,2) with dim H = 3 and all 142 essential Horn inequalities strict shows. Everything else at this rank is settled: intrinsic dimension at most two by Ehrhart reciprocity, and the coefficients of t^6 down to t^2 of a full-dimensional hive by the codimension 0 to 4 atlases (minima 1/264 at codimension three and 739/86400 at codimension four after the slack closure). Completeness of the reduction rests on the dilation lemma and on the local formula, both in print, and on the finiteness of the projected atlas for item (b), which is the obligation this move records. The deduction back to the claim of this attack: W(5) and item (b) give every coefficient of every five-part hive, hence the rung; the parent attack then owes every rank above five.

action: Plan step 3, entry actions 1 and 2. Prediction, from the study's item 4: because a valid McMullen local formula assigns to each face a weight depending only on its transverse cone type, and because that type is determined by the set of outward primitive normals of the facets containing the face, the identity a_1(P) = sum over the edges E of P of w(type(E)) times the lattice length of E is one linear equation in the unknown weights for every hive polytope, with a right-hand side this project has already certified; so the weights at codimension five, for which no closed formula and no distributed implementation exists, could be determined from the recorded Ehrhart data rather than from the Berline-Vergne recursion, and any weight the data pins is the value of every valid local formula there, whatever construction produced it. Test, as deterministic/certified-special-case-check-1: build the extraction (localform.py over hivepoly.py: outward primitive normals from Normaliz's support hyperplanes, faces from its face lattice with its volumes, edges from vertex pairs whose common tight facets have rank five with the lattice length read from the primitive direction vector) and check it where the weight is known, by recomputing the top three Ehrhart coefficients of 2,000 full-dimensional five-part hive polytopes from the faces of codimension 0, 1 and 2 and comparing with the coefficients the box attack certified. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary against its files; 200 right-hand sides against the lrcalc-pinned records of enumeration-run-2; the edges of 20 polytopes recomputed from Normaliz's face lattice with its own one-dimensional volumes, against the run's vertex-pair extraction; and the weight formula's self-test rewritten in the checker.
output: The prediction's mechanism is confirmed and its cost is measured. All 2,000 polytopes agree exactly on a_6, a_5 and a_4, with 0 mismatches, so the local formula transferred to the rational hive polytope, the outward-normal and relative-volume conventions, and the extraction are correct, and the same machinery may be used at codimension five where the weight is unknown. The measurement corrects the plan: those 2,000 polytopes have 133,188 edges in 8,305 distinct types, so the linear system that would determine the weights has four times as many unknowns as equations, and the type count grows with the number of polytopes (2,743 types at 400 polytopes, 8,305 at 2,000), so more data alone does not pin the weights. The unknowns are not independent: the weight is an invariant of the transverse cone up to lattice isometry, and the Gram matrix of the normal set up to permutation, a necessary invariant, already collapses 8,305 types to 2,628 classes and the 3,876 types of size five to 1,288. Corrected prediction for the next step: the weights are determined by the recorded data only after the types are merged by explicit lattice isometries of the ambient Z^6, which must be exhibited rather than assumed since equality of Gram matrices is necessary and not obviously sufficient; the merged system is then to be solved exactly, its pinned coordinates read off, and their signs decided. The other outputs bounding the next step: the 27 primitive rhombus normals of N_5 are recovered exactly, the edges carry between 5 and 10 facets, and the extraction costs about 90 milliseconds per polytope, so all 13,217 full-dimensional five-part records of the box and the 100,000 sampled beyond it are within reach.

action: Plan step 4, entry actions 1 and 2, testing the corrected prediction of move 2 by an exact computation, as deterministic/symbolic-computation-run-1. The 8,305 edge types of the previous step were merged into isometry classes of (Z^6, standard inner product) by tools/isotypes.py, a backtracking search for the lexicographically least image under the 46,080 signed permutations, which is legitimate because a local weight is invariant under lattice isometries whatever construction produced it; the merge gives 3,406 classes. The system of one equation per polytope, a_1(P) = sum over the edges of the weight of the edge's class times its lattice length, was then reduced exactly over the rationals by sparse Gauss-Jordan elimination. A side experiment generated 200 generic polytopes with the same 27 rhombus normals and random integral right-hand sides, to see whether polytopes outside the hive family are a better source of equations. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the rank and the pinned count recomputed modulo 2^31 - 1 by an elimination sharing no code with the exact one; the counts recomputed from the raw edge data; and explicit signed permutations exhibited for 40 merged classes.
output: The route fails, for a structural reason, and the failure is measured rather than guessed. Of the 2,000 polytopes only 466 give distinct equations, because many canonical triples of the box carry the same hive polytope up to lattice equivalence; the rank is 442 against 3,406 unknowns; not one class is pinned; and no equation contradicts another after the merge, which is evidence that the merge itself is right. More data does not close the gap in the way move 2's prediction assumed: each polytope gives one equation but touches hundreds of classes, and the classes grow with the sample (2,743 types at 400 polytopes, 8,305 at 2,000). Generic polytopes are worse, not better: of 200 with random integral right-hand sides for the 27 rhombus inequalities only one has an Ehrhart quasi-polynomial of period one, and that one has 351 edges in 351 distinct classes. The corrected plan is therefore that the codimension-five weights must be computed and not fitted: the defining local Euler-Maclaurin recursion has to be implemented here, since no closed formula exists above dimension three and the source's dimension-four script is not distributed, and validated against the closed formulas in dimensions two and three and against this project's certified coefficients, which the extraction of move 2 already reproduces exactly. Two positive by-products stand: the isometry merge is available and cheap, 8,305 types to 3,406 classes in twelve seconds with explicit witnesses, and it will cut the atlas the recursion has to evaluate by the same factor; and the extraction is validated, so the recursion's output can be tested by the same identity on 2,000 polytopes at codimension two before it is trusted at codimension five.

action: Plan step 5, entry action 1 (two independent computations of the same quantity, compared exactly), applied to the object move 3 showed must be computed rather than fitted: the local weight of a cone in dimensions four and five, for which no closed formula is in print and the source's script is not distributed. The construction was read from the primary source rather than reconstructed: Berline and Vergne, arXiv:math/0507256, Proposition 4.1, whose LaTeX was fetched and read, gives the unique family mu with mu({0}) = 1 and S(a) = sum over the faces f of a of mu(t(a,f)) I(f); isolating the vertex term makes it a recursion on the dimension, and evaluating along a generic line makes every term a Laurent series in one variable with exact rational coefficients whose poles cancel. tools/bvweight.py implements this for simplicial cones, with the saturation and the quotient lattice bases computed by an augmented Hermite reduction so that they are saturated by construction, and deterministic/certified-special-case-check-2 computes the weight on twenty cones of dimensions one to five. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass), every identity rewritten in the checker: the half-line is 1/2; the closed formula of Castillo-Liu Lemma 3.3 on six two-dimensional cones; the four vertex weights of the unit square sum to the Ehrhart constant term 1; the valuation property on a cone of index three, subdivided along an interior ray into two unimodular cones, which tests the non-unimodular case where no closed formula applies; the closed formula of Castillo-Liu Lemma 3.10 on five three-dimensional cones including one of index two; the orthants in dimensions four and five against the powers of 1/2; and multiplicativity over orthogonal sums for cones splitting as 2 + 2 and 2 + 3 against the products of the closed formulas.
output: The obstruction that closed the fitting route is removed: the local weight is now computable at the dimension this rung needs, in exact arithmetic, at under a second per five-dimensional cone, and it agrees with everything in print where the two overlap (eight checks in dimensions one to three) and with the two structural identities that reach dimensions four and five (the orthants 1/16 and 1/32, and multiplicativity over orthogonal sums, 9/64 and 15/128). Sample values at the target dimension: an irreducible five-dimensional cone has weight 63/256 and one of index two has 1/16. The cost of the whole rank-five edge atlas is therefore about forty minutes for its 3,406 isometry classes, which move 3 produced. Two things stand between this and the rung. First, the conversion from an edge's normal set to its transverse cone: the cone is the polar of the normal cone inside the span of the normals, and its lattice is the projection of Z^6, so the atlas has to be rewritten in the projected coordinates before the weight is applied. Second, the edges whose normal cone has more than five extreme rays, which are 4,429 of the 8,305 types, where the transverse cone is not simplicial and must be triangulated, the weight being a valuation. Both are mechanical; neither is a new mathematical input.

action: Plan step 4, entry actions 1, 2 and 5, on the finite list the rung reduces to. tools/transverse.py was written to convert a class of the atlas, given by the outward normals of the facets through an edge, to its transverse cone: the polar of the normal cone inside the span of the normals, carrying the projection of Z^6 as its lattice, in coordinates of a basis of that projected lattice with its Gram matrix; the conversion was checked at codimension two, where it reproduces the closed pair formula on twelve faces of a hive polytope, and end to end, where the local formula with the computed weights reproduces the certified linear coefficients 89/30 and 13/4 of two hive polytopes exactly. deterministic/enumeration-run-1 then computed the Berline-Vergne weight of every one of the 3,406 isometry classes, triangulating the 1,898 non-simplicial transverse cones by Normaliz without new rays and summing with the inclusion-exclusion of the valuation property. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary against the atlas file; 135 classes whose cone and lattice split into unimodular blocks of dimension at most three checked against the products of the closed formulas of Castillo-Liu, 0 mismatches; the end-to-end identity on five hive polytopes, 0 mismatches; and the same identity on a polytope realising each negative class, 5 checked, 0 mismatches.
output: The termwise route is closed at this rung, by an explicit finding rather than a difficulty. Five of the 3,406 classes have a negative Berline-Vergne weight, the minimum being -347/109824 and the maximum over all classes 906853/3628800; all five cones are simplicial with five rays, and each is the full normal cone of an edge of an explicit five-part hive polytope of the box: class 308 with weight -19/12096 occurs in 129 of the 2,000 polytopes, for instance at lam = (13,5,4,3,2), mu = (8,3,2,1), nu = (7,3,2,1) with two such edges, and the other four occur at (11,6,5,4,1),(7,4,3,1),(6,3,2,1), (10,7,5,4,1),(7,3,2,1),(6,4,3,1), (10,7,5,4,1),(7,4,3,1),(5,4,2,1) and (9,7,5,4,2),(6,4,3,1),(6,4,2,1). Every host polytope still has a positive linear coefficient, so the negative weights are outweighed. This is the analogue at codimension five of what Ferudun 2026 records at codimension four, with the difference that matters: his negative four-normal cells cannot be full normal cones of hive faces and are repaired by a slack closure, whereas these five are full normal cones of genuine edges, so no closure repairs them. The consequence for the rung is exact: the argument that proved the top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive and the coefficient of t^2 at rank five cannot be continued to the linear coefficient cell by cell with this local formula. What survives is Ferudun's (HTE): a McMullen local formula is not unique, and its rank-five instance is now a finite linear program with an explicit base point, the 3,406 weights recorded here, whose unknowns are the freedom of the boundary map. Two by-products stand: the weight is computable at this dimension at about two seconds per class, so any successor formula can be evaluated on the same atlas; and the end-to-end identity gives a test that any candidate formula must pass, reproducing certified coefficients of real hive polytopes.

action: Plan step 2 again, a second residue after move 5 closed the termwise one. The residue is the chamber complex rather than the cone atlas. Write a triple as b and the hive polytope as H(b) = {x : A x + C b >= 0} with A the thirty rhombus rows in the six interior entries and C their boundary parts. The cell through b0 is the set of b at which every row tight at a vertex of H(b0) stays tight and every row slack at a vertex stays satisfied, intersected with the dominance inequalities and |lam| = |mu| + |nu|; it is a rational cone holding b0 in its relative interior, and there are finitely many cells because a cell is the finite datum of which rows are tight at which vertex. On the relative interior of a cell the polytope keeps its face lattice, every vertex is a fixed linear function of b, every edge keeps its transverse cone and has a lattice length linear in b, so the local Euler-Maclaurin formula makes a1 a linear functional there; the same follows from Rassart's piecewise polynomiality (arXiv:math/0308101) together with the homogeneity a_k(m b) = m^k a_k(b), which holds because the stretched polynomial of m b is the stretched polynomial of b at m t. Hence a1 >= 0 on the whole of a cell if and only if the functional is nonnegative at the cell's extreme rays, and the size of the triples does not survive into the residue. deterministic/certified-special-case-check-3 built the cell through each of the 2000 certified full-dimensional five-part hive polytopes of certified-special-case-check-1, computed its extreme rays by the dual algorithm of Normaliz, computed the functional by finite differences of certified Ehrhart coefficients at the sum of the rays, which is in the relative interior, and read off the minimum. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary and each cell's minimum recomputed from the records; the certified coefficient carried by each cell against the value recorded by certified-special-case-check-1; every extreme ray verified to be a triple of partitions of equal size and every cell's own triple to be a nonnegative combination of its rays; and, on a sample of cells, the ray values recomputed without Normaliz by the depth-first hive enumerator through the counts at t = 0..6 and an exact polynomial fit.
output: A second residue, and the first result of this project that is not about a bounded set of triples. 2005 cells, 1346 of them distinct, all simplicial, of rank 3 to 8: 9129 extreme rays evaluated, none negative, minimum 0 and maximum 277/60, with 7103 of the ray values exactly zero. Every cell passes its internal tests: the functional is linear along the sampled rays at two successive steps, the ray values sum to the certified coefficient at the interior point, the cell's own triple is a nonnegative combination of the rays and the functional gives it the coefficient the box certified, and all 6015 spot checks at random interior lattice points agree. So the linear coefficient is nonnegative not at 2000 points but on 1346 unbounded cones of rank 3 to 8 through them; rank one would have been no gain, since homogeneity already covers the ray through a certified triple. Where the method stops is recorded too: cells at generic points are full dimensional, of rank 14, with hundreds of extreme rays and a smallest interior point far beyond what the certified Ehrhart run can handle, so this step reaches none of them. That is the next step's job, and it needs the functional to come from the local formula and the atlas of enumeration-run-1 rather than from Ehrhart differences. The number of cells of the complex is unknown, so the reduction is exact while the enumeration of its instances is not attempted.

action: Plan step 5 on the residue move 6 wrote. That step took the cell's linear functional from finite differences of certified Ehrhart coefficients, which ties the cost to the size of the triple and left the full-dimensional cells out of reach. The local Euler-Maclaurin formula gives the same functional for nothing: on a cell every edge keeps the facet normals through it, hence its transverse cone and its weight, while its lattice length is linear in the boundary triple, so l(b) is the sum over the edges of the class weight times the lattice length. tools/atlasform.py builds it, reading weights from the codimension-five atlas of enumeration-run-1 and computing and caching a weight when a class is new. deterministic/enumeration-run-2 has two phases. Phase A recomputes the functional this way on every cell of certified-special-case-check-3 and compares its value at every extreme ray with the value that step obtained from Ehrhart differences, a comparison of two computations that share no step, one counting lattice points in dilates and the other summing weights of transverse cones. Phase B sweeps full-dimensional cells at generic points of the hive cone, of any size, for a negative value at an extreme ray, which would be a family of triples with a negative linear coefficient and so a counterexample at rank five. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary and each cell's minimum recomputed from the records; every extreme ray verified to be a triple of partitions of equal size; the identity itself at a point the sweep never evaluated, the sum of a cell's extreme rays, whose linear coefficient must be the sum of the ray values, computed from the Ehrhart quasi-polynomial on the ten cells whose ray sum is smallest, with 0 mismatches; and the weights this run computed on top of the atlas, of which the 34 whose cone and lattice split into unimodular blocks agree with the products of the closed formulas of Castillo-Liu. The depth-first enumerator reached none of these cells, all twelve candidates having more hives at t = 6 than the cap of four million, which the checker records rather than works around; that route is exercised in certified-special-case-check-3, whose numbers phase A reproduces ray by ray.
output: The size wall is gone and the two routes agree exactly. Phase A: 2006 cells, 9145 extreme rays compared, no ray value differs and no value at a cell's own triple differs, so the local formula reproduces every number the certified Ehrhart route gave. Phase B: 193 cells, every one of rank 14, built at triples of size 28,936 to 722,265, with a median of 221,438; 4764 extreme rays evaluated, none negative, minimum 0 and maximum 4067/60, and 3900 of the values are nonzero. The previous step reached one full-dimensional cell out of 24,571 attempts; this one reaches 193 in 2242 seconds, at triples five orders of magnitude larger than the box the original problem asks about. The cost per cell is the edge enumeration and the weights of classes not yet seen, 1457 of which were computed here on top of the atlas's 3406, and neither depends on the size of the triple. No negative value appeared, which is the outcome the conjecture predicts; had one appeared, the interior points of that cell near the ray would have been triples with a negative linear coefficient. What the sweep does not give is coverage: the number of full-dimensional cells of the rank-five chamber complex is unknown, so 193 is a sample of unknown density, and 1540 further sampled triples were skipped, 731 of them because they lie on a wall.

action: Plan step 5 again, sharpening the residue rather than adding samples to it. On a cell the functional is the sum over the edges of the class weight times the lattice length, and the lattice length is a nonnegative linear function of the boundary triple on the whole cell, because the edge exists with that length at every triple of the cell. So a cell all of whose edge classes have nonnegative weight satisfies l >= 0 on all of it with no computation, and the residue is only the cells that carry an edge of a negative-weight class. deterministic/certified-special-case-check-4 classifies every cell the project has built, the 2006 of certified-special-case-check-3 and the 193 of enumeration-run-2, by whether it carries such an edge, records at the worst such ray the positive part of the functional against the negative part, and recomputes the negative classes over every weight the project holds rather than over the atlas alone. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary recomputed from the records; the negative classes recomputed by canonical form from both weight files with a conflict test between them; the reduction's premise against the two steps that built the cells, that a cell with no negative-weight edge has no negative ray value there and that a cell with one has its worst-ray split equal to a recorded ray value; and the Ehrhart value at the ray sum of the eight smallest cells that carry a negative class.
output: The residue shrinks and the list of dangerous classes grows. Of 2199 cells and 226,740 edges, 732 edges are of a negative-weight class and 332 cells carry one, so 1867 cells, 85 percent, are settled by the reduction without evaluating anything. The recomputed ray values agree with both earlier steps in every case. The correction is that the negative classes are not the five of enumeration-run-1: over the 5142 classes the project now holds, 21 are negative, the most negative still -347/109824, and the two weight files agree on every class they share. The measurement that matters is the margin: at the worst ray of the worst cell the positive part of the functional is 249 times the negative part, the cell being the one at (62780,54763,54405,44759,27943), (19723,19430,11042,9184,1), (45337,45138,43238,34944,16613) with ratio 15181/61. That is where a proof would go: a bound saying the positive weight adjacent to a negative-weight edge exceeds it would close the rung, and 249 is the first evidence about how much room such a bound has. What is still not enumerated is the residue itself, since the number of cells of the chamber complex, and of those carrying a negative-weight edge, is unknown.

action: Plan step 2 on the local-configurations branch, opening pass 2. The residue after move 8 is the cells carrying an edge of a negative-weight class, and those cells are still not enumerable. A local inequality would remove the need. Give each positive-weight edge an equal share of its weighted length to each negative-weight edge in a chosen neighbourhood of it, and let share(e) be what e receives; the shares of distinct negative edges are disjoint parts of the positive sum, so share(e) >= |w(e)| times the lattice length of e, for every negative edge, gives l >= 0 on every cell at once with no cell enumerated. Both sides are linear on a cell, so each test is decided at the extreme rays. deterministic/certified-special-case-check-5 measured two neighbourhoods on all 332 cells that carry a negative edge: the vertex neighbourhood, the edges sharing a vertex with e, and the facet neighbourhood, the edges lying on a facet through e, which is the neighbourhood the class of e already names since a class is the set of facet normals through the edge. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary recomputed from the records; the cell and edge counts against certified-special-case-check-4; and, on 25 sampled cells recomputed from the polytope, the local-formula identity at every ray against the value the step that built the cell recorded from a different route, the soundness of the discharging rule, and the domination itself.
output: One neighbourhood is too small and the next one is not, by a wide margin. Over 14,899 ray tests on 332 cells and 732 negative edges, the vertex neighbourhood fails 106 times, and the failure is sharp rather than marginal: at the worst ray the share is zero, so every edge meeting the negative edge at a vertex has zero length there while the negative edge does not, and what keeps the coefficient nonnegative is positive weight further away. No argument that looks only at the edges through a vertex can work. The facet neighbourhood fails no test, and the share exceeds the demand by a factor of at least 1567265857/18738000, about 83.6, and by up to about 26,977. This turns the rung into a statement with no cell and no size in it: for every five-part hive polytope and every edge whose class has negative weight, the shared weighted length of the positive-weight edges on a facet through it is at least |w| times its lattice length. The conjecture implies the rung by the disjointness of the shares, and what it needs is a lower bound on the lengths of the edges of a facet in terms of the length of one edge on it, which is a question about the geometry of the hive polytope rather than about Ehrhart theory. The measurement covers the cells this project has built, so it says the facet neighbourhood is the right size to try to prove something about; it does not prove the conjecture.

action: The same entry again, with the neighbourhood replaced by the facet itself. Every edge f lies on c(f) facets; give each facet containing f the amount w(f) times the lattice length of f divided by c(f). Summed over the facets these shares are exactly the functional, nothing left over and nothing counted twice, so l >= 0 follows as soon as every facet pays for its own negative edges: the sum over the negative edges e on F of |w(e)| len(e)/c(e) is at most the sum over the positive edges f on F of w(f) len(f)/c(f). That mentions no cell, no chamber complex and no size, and a facet of a five-part hive polytope is again cut out by rhombus rows, so it has finitely many types. It is stronger than the neighbourhood statement of move 9, a facet being smaller than the union of the facets through an edge, and sufficient for the rung in the same way. Both sides are linear on a cell, so the test is decided at the extreme rays. deterministic/certified-special-case-check-6 ran it on every cell the project has built. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary recomputed from the records; the count of cells carrying a negative edge against certified-special-case-check-4; and, on 20 sampled cells recomputed from the polytope, that the facet shares add up at every ray to the value the step that built the cell recorded from a different route, which is what makes the per-facet inequality sufficient, and that every facet carrying a negative edge pays for it at every ray.
output: The inequality holds everywhere it was tested, and it is now a statement about a single facet. 2199 cells, 28,691 facets of which only 2556 carry a negative edge at all, 46,501 ray tests, no failure, and the ratio of the positive share to the negative one never below 4730093/276213, about 17.1. The tightest case is a facet of the hive polytope at (147770,147594,105002,70327,61221), (106246,91584,45436,31078), (100523,84659,41706,30682), one of the large cells; the small cells of certified-special-case-check-3 are far from tight, their worst ratio being about 157. The shares were also verified to add up to the functional at every ray of every sampled cell, which is what makes the per-facet form sufficient rather than merely suggestive. So the rung now has a candidate proof route with no chamber complex in it: bound below the lengths of the positive-weight edges of a facet by the lengths of its negative-weight edges. What is not done is the enumeration of the facet types of a five-part hive polytope, which is what would turn the measurement into a proof.

action: Plan step 2 on the second half of the rung, the non-full-dimensional hives, which the record has owed since move 2. A derivation with no computation in it, written to study/non-full-dimensional-reduction.md. Let H be the hive polytope in R^6 with dim H = d < 6, let L be the direction space of its affine hull and Lambda = Z^6 ∩ L, a lattice of rank d. Since the coefficient is positive there is x0 in H ∩ Z^6, and for every t the set tH ∩ Z^6 is t x0 plus t(H - x0) ∩ Lambda, because a point t x0 + z with z in L is integral exactly when z is in Z^6 ∩ L. So P(t) is the Ehrhart function of the d-dimensional rational polytope H - x0 in the rank-d lattice Lambda. That is the intrinsic-lattice contraction the record owed.
output: The second obligation of the rung is cheaper than the first, and the machinery already built applies to it unchanged. Everything proved for the full-dimensional case is a statement about a polytope and its lattice and uses no ambient rank, so the cell reduction, the nonnegative-class lemma, the discharging rule and the per-facet identity all hold for (H - x0, Lambda). What does not carry over is the atlas: the transverse cone of an edge lives in a quotient of Lambda and its normals are the images of the rhombus normals under the projection onto L, not elements of N_5. The work then divides by the intrinsic dimension d, because the transverse cone of an edge has dimension d - 1: d at most 2 is already proved by reciprocity, d = 3 needs only the closed pair formula, d = 4 only the closed formula of Castillo-Liu at dimension three, and d = 5 needs four-dimensional weights, one dimension below the five-dimensional ones the full-dimensional case needed, for which tools/bvweight.py is built and validated. The missing input is the list of transverse cone types of the projected lattices, which nobody has enumerated here; enumerating it is a bounded computational task, so it is recorded as a proposal in ADMISSION.md under the interim directive of 2026-09-05 and is not started in this move. The derivation proves no weight nonnegative and changes nothing about the full-dimensional residue.

action: A decision-guiding search, approved with amendments by two independent reviews of 2026-09-05 under the interim directive, with the predictions registered in ADMISSION.md before any result was read. Phase one built cells above the top band already measured, from both sources so that edge count and construction route are separated, with the vertex cap raised from 220 to 600, and tested the per-facet inequality at every extreme ray of each. Phase two answered the question the search could not: the trend reading's stated mechanism is that the negative share grows with the number of negative edges on a facet, and facets.jsonl records no per-facet detail, so refacet.py re-ran the facet computation over the 2,119 cells already built and recorded, for every facet carrying a negative edge, how many it carries. The run was stopped at its allowance with one cell in progress; summarise.py is the summary block of run.py run separately over the 242 complete records. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): both summaries recomputed from their records including the failure count; the band table's old rows recomputed from certified-special-case-check-6 and merged with the new; the per-facet inequality recomputed from the polytope on eight sampled new cells; and the mechanism medians regrouped without trusting the run's own grouping.
output: The alarm was mine and it was wrong, and the experiment says why. Phase one: 242 cells, 70 of them above 684 edges and 38 of those built at generic points against 32 from perturbed box triples, 206,072 facet ray tests of which 157,814 above 684 edges, largest cell 1,127 edges, no failing facet, worst ratio 14.89. On the registered criterion that is undecided: the top band's median is 27.14 against the trend reading's 40, but on three cells, while the 70 cells above 684 edges have medians 63.73 generic and 93.48 from box triples, both between the two predictions and differing from each other at matched edge count, which is the provenance effect. Phase two decides the mechanism. Over 1,892 facets carrying a negative edge, the median ratio by the number of negative edges on the facet is 644.91, 406.18, 298.90, 174.22, 237.78, 135.76 and 280.43 for counts one to seven, a spread of 4.75, while by the cell's edge count it is 717.20, 617.00, 533.13 and 446.87, a spread of 1.60 over an eightfold growth; by cell rank the spread is 1.34 and by source 1.22. So the driver is the number of negative edges on a facet and not the size of the cell, and the fall of the per-cell worst ratio from 273.77 to 83.93 across the bands is mostly the order-statistic effect of taking a minimum over more facets. The doubt therefore moves: not whether complexity breaks the inequality, but whether a facet can carry many negative edges at once, the observed maximum being seven with a median ratio still 135.76 at six. Extrapolating the reciprocal trend, a failure needs a facet carrying of order hundreds. The per-facet inequality remains unproved and no number of passing facets proves it.

action: An analysis with no new computation, regrouping the records enumeration-run-3 already wrote and recording it as deterministic/enumeration-run-3/mediation.py and mediation.json with an addendum to that step's README. Move 12 read two groupings of per-facet.jsonl side by side and concluded that the driver of the margin is the per-facet negative-edge count and not the size of the cell. This move separates the two questions the side-by-side reading conflated: how the count itself varies with the cell, and whether the count still moves the margin once the cell's size is held fixed.
output: Move 12's wording was too strong and is corrected. The count grows with the cell: by edge-count band the maximum count is 1, 3, 7, 6 and the mean is 1.00, 1.10, 1.63, 1.77, while the share of facets carrying three or more negative edges goes 0.000, 0.001, 0.139, 0.201. And inside the 512-edge band alone, with the cell's size held fixed, the count still moves the margin, the median ratio falling 589.29, 432.29, 266.13, 234.25, 187.78, 135.76 for counts one to six. So the count is the proximate driver and the cell's size acts on the margin through it; both effects are real and they compose, rather than the second being absent. What does not change is the size of the effects. The mean count grows about as the cell's edge count to the power 0.35 and the median ratio falls about as the count to the power 0.85, so a facet whose margin reaches one needs a count of order two thousand, and a cell with that mean count would need of order ten million edges against the 1,127 actually built. On this evidence the per-facet inequality is robust, its failure point being far outside anything reachable, and it remains unproved. The correction matters for the record rather than for the route: the next question is still how many negative-weight edges one facet can carry, and it is now known to be a quantity that grows, slowly, with the cell.

action: A repair move. An independent review audited the executed moves 12 and 13 and found two defects in evidence that had already passed its checker. First, refacet.py stops at a time budget and its first pass covered 2,119 of the 2,199 cells, omitting the last 80, all from enumeration-run-2 and all among the largest, which carry 664 of the 2,556 facets that hold a negative edge; so the tables that retired the complexity alarm omitted 26 percent of the relevant facets and exactly the ones where the counts are highest, and the step's own checker regrouped the same truncated file and could not catch it. Second, the addendum's extrapolated failure point of ten million edges does not follow from the addendum's own fits. The repair re-ran the mechanism pass over all 2,199 cells in 478 seconds, kept the truncated output as per-facet.truncated.jsonl and per-facet.truncated.summary.json, recomputed the mediation tables, rewrote the phase-two section and the addendum of the step's README with the full population, added the fit exponents and the ranges the fits are extended beyond, and re-verified the step, which passes.
output: The conclusion of move 12 survives the repair and is slightly stronger, and the extrapolation of move 13 was wrong by four orders of magnitude. On the full population of 2,199 cells and 2,556 facets carrying a negative edge, the median ratio spreads by 6.20 across the per-facet negative-edge count, against 4.75 on the truncated data, and by 1.55 across an eightfold growth of the cell, against 1.60; so the count is still the proximate driver and by a wider margin. Two bins contradict the trend and are now recorded rather than smoothed: five negative edges gives 333.69, above the value at four, and the single facet with seven gives 280.43, above the value at six. The corrected extrapolation: fitting the full population, the mean count grows about as the cell's edge count to the power 0.31 and the median ratio falls about as the count to the power 0.94, so the median margin reaches one at a per-facet count of order 800 and a cell with that mean count has of order 2 times 10 to the 11 edges. The earlier figure of ten million came from extrapolating the worst ratio, the order statistic the same document calls an artefact, and is withdrawn. Both fits run far outside their data, the count fit from 1.00 to 1.70 over four bands extended to 800 and the ratio fit over six bins whose last two hold 8 and 4 facets extended to a count of 800, and the record now says so beside each. What this changes for the route is nothing; what it changes for the record is that a passed checker did not catch a truncated input, which is the reason the checker now reads the full file.

action: The first move that changes the weight instead of arguing around it, approved with eleven amendments by two independent reviews. Every route since move 8 works around the same twenty-one classes of negative Berline-Vergne weight, and the nonnegative-class lemma says that if no class is negative the coefficient is nonnegative on every cell with no computation at all. Berline and Vergne construct their formula for polytopes in a rational euclidean space, so the scalar product is a parameter and any rational positive-definite form is admissible; tools/bvweight.py already takes the Gram matrix as an argument. deterministic/enumeration-run-4 ran the first gate that amendment 3 requires: for a lattice polytope the local formula read at codimension equal to the dimension says the weights of the tangent cones at the vertices sum to one, which is exact and needs no Ehrhart computation. Two polytopes, the unimodular six-simplex with seven tangent cones and the unit six-cube with sixty-four signed orthants; four forms, the standard one, twice the standard one as the scale-invariance control, the A_6 root-lattice form chosen because its automorphism group is large so a usable collapse of edge types survives, and the form with unit diagonal and off-diagonal one quarter. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the recorded sums and vertex counts; the same identity on a second, non-unimodular lattice simplex the run did not use; the scale invariance the classification argument rests on, on random three-dimensional cones; and the closed value two to the minus six on signed orthants under the standard form.
output: The family is real and the code is now validated one dimension higher. The standard form, twice the standard form and the A_6 form each give one on both polytopes, sixty-four signed orthants included; the fourth form was cut at sixteen of sixty-four by the allowance and is undecided. So a form other than the standard one passes the necessary test, which is what the whole programme needed before spending anything on it. Two by-products: the weight code is validated in dimension six, where it had been validated only to dimension five, since the standard form reproduces two to the minus six on the orthants and the identity closes to one over sixty-four of them; and scale invariance, which the classification argument in the admission record rests on, is confirmed rather than assumed. What this does not show is stated in the step: the gate is necessary and not sufficient, nothing here says the A_6 weights are a valid local formula for every polytope, and nothing here touches the twenty-one negative classes. That is the next phase and it needs its own allowance, because the transverse cone of an edge has to be built in the form's own orthogonal complement and tools/transverse.py does that only for the standard form. A six-dimensional weight costs about 6.3 seconds, so the thirty-minute allowance bought three forms and part of a fourth, and it is spent.

action: The screen the fourth review required, in the order it required: the cheap five-dimensional evaluation of the twenty-one negative representatives and of a control of the ten smallest positive weights held, over a list of forms declared in forms.py before the run, with the expensive codimension-six vertex-sum gate left for later. transverse_q.py makes the projection and the Gram depend on the form; the span of the face is the common kernel of the normals and stays metric-free, and the inequalities are dual pairings and stay unchanged. Because the vertex-sum gate of enumeration-run-4 is at codimension six and validates the path that is not changing, two checks ran first: recorded weights reproduced exactly under the standard form, and the codimension-five identity on the unimodular six-simplex, whose Ehrhart polynomial is C(t+6,6) so that its twenty-one edges, each of lattice length one, carry weights summing to H_6 = 49/20. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the recorded counts recomputed from the weight lists; the identity recomputed for two forms with the simplex's edges taken from the polytope by Normaliz instead of from the hand-written normal sets; the module against recorded weights on a fresh disjoint sample; and the classes surviving the best form recomputed under it.
output: The negativity is largely an artefact of the standard scalar product and not wholly, and the residue of this route drops from twenty-one classes to five. Every one of the ten forms passes the codimension-five identity at 49/20, which is the necessary validity test at the codimension that matters and is also a new validation of the module. Under the standard form all twenty-one are negative and the control is clean. The root-lattice forms trade rather than fix: A_6 and D_6 lift five and push all ten control classes negative, E_6 lifts three and does the same, which is what the review predicted when it required the control to be the smallest positive weights rather than a random sample. Their duals do better, lifting fourteen at the cost of two. The best is a single small perturbation, the identity with every off-diagonal entry one quarter, which lifts sixteen of the twenty-one and leaves all ten control classes positive; one half behaves the same, and minus one eighth is worse than the standard form. Five classes survive every form tried and the checker recomputed them under the best form. What is not claimed is recorded with it: ten forms are a finite sample of a twenty-one-parameter continuum; only the standard form and A_6 have passed the codimension-six gate, and the two best forms are not among them; lifting a representative is not lifting its class, since a non-standard form breaks the collapse by signed permutations; and a form that lifted all twenty-one would still need the other 5,121 held classes re-evaluated under it.

action: The first step of amendment 2 of the fifth independent review, run before any solve because it either yields a barrier for nothing or shows the solve is not worth starting. The review observed that requiring a local formula to be nonnegative and to reproduce every recorded linear coefficient reads as A w' = a1 with A entrywise nonnegative, its entries the lattice lengths, and the right-hand side nonnegative; a row of value zero then forces w' to vanish on that row's support, 7,109 of the recorded ray values are zero, and if a row of positive value had its support inside the union of the zero supports the system would be infeasible with no solver at all. deterministic/certified-special-case-check-8 tested the premise that argument needs, on every extreme ray of every cell the project has built. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary recomputed from the records; the row counts against the ray counts recorded by the steps that built the cells; and, on sampled cells, the lengths recomputed from the polytope, with the recorded ray value checked against the sum over the edges of the weight times the length.
output: The shortcut is vacuous and the forty-five minutes it would have cost are not spent. Over 2,199 cells and 13,909 rows, 7,973 rows have value zero and not one of them has a non-empty support: at a ray where the linear coefficient vanishes the hive polytope degenerates to a point, every edge has length zero, and the row imposes nothing. The 5,936 rows of positive value all have a non-empty support, and no edge has negative length at any row, which confirms the two structural facts the linear program rests on, that the matrix is entrywise nonnegative and that no positive row is empty. What this leaves is a weaker prospect than the review's structural argument suggested: infeasibility, if reachable, must come from the equality relations rather than from the sign pattern, and move 3 of this attack already measured that side at 466 distinct equations of rank 442 against 3,406 unknowns with the class count growing faster than the equation count. The record says so before the run rather than after it.

action: Settling in writing, before a move was spent on it, the question amendment 2 of the sixth review required: whether the positivity statements this project holds at codimensions two and three are about every cone of those dimensions or only about cones whose normals lie in the rank-five normal set. Move 11 had reduced obligation O-B to the same problem one dimension lower, so intrinsic dimension three needs two-dimensional weights and intrinsic dimension four needs three-dimensional ones, and if the positivity were general those dimensions would close outright through the nonnegative-class lemma with no enumeration. The test is seconds of arithmetic on toy cones with tools/bvweight.py, recorded as accounting in study/low-dimensional-weights-can-be-negative.md rather than as a run.
output: The shortcut is unavailable, and the general statement is false. Under the standard form the two-dimensional cone with rays (1,0) and (-5,1) has weight -19/104, the one with rays (1,0) and (-20,1) has -2279/1604, and the one with rays (20,1) and (-20,1) has -2279/802, while thin cones go the other way and (1,0) with (100,1) has weight above eight. So the Berline-Vergne weight of a two-dimensional cone is negative as soon as the cone is wide enough, and negativity does not begin at dimension four as the record's earlier reading of the rank-five families suggested. It is consistent with the identity the weights satisfy: for a lattice polygon the vertex weights sum to one, so a polygon with many vertices cannot have every weight bounded below by a positive constant, and nothing forces nonnegativity. The consequence for O-B is exact: the positivity at codimensions two and three in this record is about the cones spanned by the twenty-seven rank-five rhombus normals, not about all cones of those dimensions, and the projected lattices produce normals that are images of those rather than elements of the set, so O-B needs its own atlas at each intrinsic dimension exactly as the full-dimensional case did. What move 11 established still stands: the reductions carry over unchanged and the hardest case needs four-dimensional weights, one dimension below what the full-dimensional case needed.

action: The projected atlas of obligation O-B, approved with seven amendments by the seventh review, which are all incorporated. Move 11 reduced O-B to the same problem in the intrinsic lattice one dimension lower and move 18 removed the shortcut that would have closed the low dimensions by citation, so each intrinsic dimension needs its own atlas. contract.py translates the polytope by a lattice point of it, takes the lattice of the linear span saturated in the ambient lattice, expresses the polytope and the hive rows in a basis of it and carries the induced Gram; transverse_q.py then builds the transverse cones with that Gram in place of the identity. The review's central catch is that the end-to-end identity tests validity and cannot see the Gram, since every positive-definite form gives a valid local formula, so a wrong form would reproduce the certified coefficient exactly while changing the sign census; the contraction is therefore checked directly, that the intrinsic lattice is saturated, that the basis generates it rather than a sublattice, that the Gram is recomputed from ambient inner products and that it is positive definite. Independent checker (check.sh, harness status pass): the summary recomputed from the records; the identity recomputed from scratch with no cache on sampled contracted polytopes; the contraction checks on those; and the seven two-dimensional weights of move 18 with the polygon identity on the unimodular triangle, recomputed because a route decision rests on them.
output: No projected type at intrinsic dimension three or four has a negative weight. 444,175 polytopes contracted, 391,961 of them validated by the end-to-end identity with no mismatch, 38,899 distinct types keyed by the normal set together with the intrinsic Gram, of which 1,400 at intrinsic dimension three, 11,934 at four and 25,565 at five; 13,334 weighed at dimensions three and four, none negative, the smallest weight 1/120 and the largest 17/42. By the nonnegative-class lemma that covers, for the types seen, every coefficient at intrinsic dimension three, since a_3 is the volume, a_2 half the facet volumes, a_1 this atlas and a_0 one; and at intrinsic dimension four everything but a_2, which needs the codimension-two atlas of the two-faces that this run did not build. Intrinsic dimension five is enumerated and not weighed, its 25,565 types needing four-dimensional weights, which is the next run. The completeness caveat is why this is coverage and not discharge: the types are those occurring in the box's contracted polytopes and the count was still growing when the allowance ended, from 33,252 at 624 seconds to 38,899 at 1,700; a complete atlas is available in principle because the intrinsic direction space is the span of a face of the hive cone and there are finitely many, but its cost is not measured. One bug is recorded because it is the reason the identity check exists: keying a type by its normal set alone gave 3,486 identity mismatches, since the weight depends on the intrinsic lattice too and two contracted polytopes can share a normal set with different lattices; keying by the normal set with the Gram took the mismatches to zero.
